themes_detail.label: Street noise surge this week
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints spiked to 51 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 14.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 261% increase (z-score: 4.9)—suggesting a sudden, acute disruption that warrants immediate investigation into construction, vendor activity, or events.
evidence: 51 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 14.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (261% spike, z-score: 4.9)
General noise complaints also elevated at 32 last week vs. 13.0 weekly average (146% spike, z-score: 6.94)
Combined noise signal (street + residential) represents most recently accelerating complaint category
reporting_angles: Interview residents on specific blocks with heaviest complaints; identify source (construction, vendors, street repair work)
Cross-reference with DOB permits filed in past 2 weeks to identify active construction; contact Department of Environmental Protection on noise enforcement

themes_detail.label: Lot condition emergency spike
themes_detail.summary: Lot condition complaints exploded to 8 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 0.4 per week—a 2033% surge (z-score: 10.96, highest statistical anomaly in dataset)—indicating either a single major blight incident or a newly reported systemic problem requiring urgent field verification.
evidence: 8 lot condition complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly average over 8 weeks (2033% spike, z-score: 10.96—highest anomaly in entire dataset)
Signal is geographically concentrated in CD 501, suggesting localized blight event rather than city-wide pattern
Aligns with CB budget requests for illegal building conversions and code enforcement (DOB)
reporting_angles: Map the 8 complaints to specific addresses; conduct on-the-ground inspection for abandoned buildings, illegal dumping, or fire damage
Interview Department of Buildings on enforcement activity in past 2 weeks; determine if complaints reflect new code violations or failures to remediate existing ones

themes_detail.label: Missing street signs and infrastructure decay
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints (specifically missing signs) jumped to 3 THIS WEEK versus 0.9 weekly baseline—a 243% spike—paired with a 465% surge in dead/dying tree complaints last week (12 vs. 2.1 avg), signaling accelerating public realm deterioration that compounds CB's recurring street light and infrastructure repair requests.
evidence: 3 missing street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average (243% spike, z-score: 3.54)
12 dead/dying tree complaints last week vs. 2.1 weekly average (465% spike, z-score: 4.87)
CB has submitted recurring budget request for street light repair/replacement (Agency: DOT)—corroborating pattern of infrastructure neglect
reporting_angles: Investigate whether DOT has deprioritized maintenance in CD 501; compare response times and budget allocation vs. other districts
Visit neighborhoods with highest complaint density; document missing signage, dead trees, and broken lights as visual evidence of deferred maintenance

themes_detail.label: Residential noise complaints elevated
themes_detail.summary: Residential noise complaints reached 32 LAST WEEK versus 13.0 weekly baseline—a 146% increase (z-score: 6.94)—suggesting either sustained disruptive activity (nightlife, construction, transit) or a shift in resident complaints that deserves scene reporting to identify patterns.
evidence: 32 residential noise complaints last week vs. 13.0 weekly average (146% spike, z-score: 6.94)
Elevation persists this week alongside street noise spike, indicating sustained rather than one-time event
No Reddit discussions or CB agenda items yet, suggesting residents may not yet be organized; window for early reporting
reporting_angles: Interview noise complaint filers by block to identify common sources (bars, nightlife, venue expansion, late-night deliveries)
Cross-check with NYPD incident data and SLA license records for bar/venue activity changes in past 3 weeks

themes_detail.label: Traffic and parking infrastructure stress
themes_detail.summary: Traffic complaints spiked to 25 THREE WEEKS AGO (326% above baseline of 5.9 weekly, z-score: 4.29), while illegal parking remains the second-highest complaint category overall at 1765 over 90 days—together these signals suggest growing congestion or a shift in vehicle enforcement that deserves investigation into transit/development-driven changes.
evidence: 25 traffic complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 5.9 weekly average (326% spike, z-score: 4.29)
1765 illegal parking complaints over 90-day period (2nd-highest category, indicating chronic structural issue)
3 active ULURP/land use applications (198-208 Richmond Terrace + 2 others) may signal incoming development-driven traffic changes
reporting_angles: Assess whether traffic spike correlates with start of construction on any of the 3 land use filings
Interview DOT on parking enforcement strategy shift; determine if spike reflects increased ticketing or genuine increase in violations
